title: The 8253 and 8254 interval timer as a chip
covers: The 8253 and 8254 programmable interval timer as a chip: its power-up state, its six counter modes and the GATE input

rows.text: The 8254 is a counter/timer with three independent 16-bit counters, each handling clock inputs up to 10 MHz.
All modes are software programmable, and the 8254 is a superset of the 8253.
Software treats the 8254 as an array of I/O ports: three counters and a fourth control register for mode programming.
After power-up the state of the 8254 is undefined: the mode, count value and output of every counter.
Each counter must be programmed before it can be used; unused counters need not be programmed.
A CLK pulse is a rising then a falling edge of CLK, a trigger is a rising edge of GATE, loading is the CR to CE transfer.
Mode 0: OUT is low after the control word and stays low until the count reaches zero, then high until a new count or control word.
Mode 0: GATE = 1 enables counting and GATE = 0 disables it; GATE has no effect on OUT.
Mode 0: the initial count loads on the next CLK pulse without decrementing, so OUT goes high N+1 pulses after the write.
Mode 0: a new count loads on the next CLK pulse; the first byte of a two-byte count disables counting and sets OUT low.
Mode 0: the second byte lets the new count load on the next CLK pulse, and OUT goes high N+1 pulses after it.
Mode 0: a count written while GATE is 0 still loads on the next CLK pulse; OUT goes high N pulses after GATE goes high.
Mode 1: OUT is high, goes low on the CLK pulse after a trigger and stays low until the counter reaches zero.
Mode 1: after the control word and count the counter is armed; a trigger loads it and sets OUT low on the next CLK pulse for N cycles.
Mode 1: the one-shot is retriggerable and can repeat without rewriting the count; GATE has no effect on OUT.
Mode 1: a new count written during a one-shot does not affect it unless it is retriggered, and then loads the new count.
Mode 2 divides by N: OUT is high, goes low for one CLK pulse when the count reaches 1, then the counter reloads and repeats.
Mode 2: GATE = 0 disables counting and sets OUT high at once; a trigger reloads the counter on the next CLK pulse.
Mode 2: after the control word and count the counter loads on the next CLK pulse and OUT goes low N pulses after the write.
Mode 2: a new count does not change the current sequence; it loads at the end of the period or after a trigger.
Mode 2: a count of 1 is illegal.
Mode 3 is a periodic square wave like mode 2: OUT is high for half the count and low for the rest, with period N CLK cycles.
Mode 3: GATE = 0 disables counting and sets OUT high at once; a trigger reloads the counter on the next CLK pulse.
Mode 3: after the control word and count the counter loads on the next CLK pulse.
Mode 3: a new count does not change the current sequence; it loads at the end of the half-cycle or after a trigger.
In modes 2 and 3 a GATE transition should not occur one clock before terminal count.
Mode 3, even count: OUT is high, the count loads on one CLK pulse and drops by two per pulse; at expiry OUT toggles and the count reloads.
Mode 3, odd count: the count minus one is loaded and drops by two; OUT is high for (N+1)/2 counts and low for (N-1)/2.
Mode 4: OUT is high and goes low for one CLK pulse when the count expires; writing the count triggers the sequence.
Mode 4: GATE = 1 enables counting and GATE = 0 disables it; GATE has no effect on OUT.
Mode 4: the count loads on the next CLK pulse and OUT strobes low N+1 pulses after the count is written.
Mode 4: a new count loads on the next CLK pulse; the first byte of a two-byte count has no effect, the second retriggers.
Mode 5: OUT is high; a rising GATE edge triggers counting, and when the count expires OUT goes low for one CLK pulse.
Mode 5: the counter loads on the CLK pulse after a trigger and OUT strobes low N+1 pulses later; it is retriggerable.
Mode 5: a new count during counting does not affect the sequence; a trigger afterwards loads it on the next CLK pulse.
GATE low disables counting in modes 0, 2, 3 and 4 and sets OUT high in modes 2 and 3; a rising edge triggers modes 1, 2, 3 and 5.
Minimum counts are 1 in modes 0, 1, 4 and 5 and 2 in modes 2 and 3; the maximum count 0 equals 2^16 binary or 10^4 BCD.
A control word written to a counter resets all its control logic at once, and OUT goes to a known initial state with no CLK pulse.
GATE is always sampled on the rising edge of CLK; in modes 0, 2, 3 and 4 it is level sensitive.
In modes 1, 2, 3 and 5 GATE is rising-edge sensitive: a trigger sets a flip-flop that the next rising CLK edge samples and resets.
In modes 2 and 3 GATE is both edge and level sensitive; with an external clock, GATE should be pulsed after WR of a new count.
New counts are loaded and counters are decremented on the falling edge of CLK.
The largest initial count is 0, equal to 2^16 for binary counting and 10^4 for BCD counting.
The counter does not stop at zero: in modes 0, 1, 4 and 5 it wraps to FFFF or 9999 and goes on; modes 2 and 3 reload.
device_reset gives every counter a defined control word, count and latch, and marks the output undetermined.
A count of 1 loads as 2 in mode 2 and as 0 in mode 3, found by experiment.
In mode 2 a count of 1 loads as 2 and in mode 3 as 0, the largest count, where the minimum is 2.
Reads and writes at offsets 0 to 3 go to counters 0 to 2 and the control word.
TIMER_Init gives every counter mode 0, count 0x10000 and a read state, so power-up is defined.
The counter value is computed from the time elapsed since the count started, not decremented per CLK pulse.
A new count takes effect at once: the count restarts from the write instead of waiting for a CLK pulse.
OUT goes low when the count reads 1, which is N-1 ticks after the write.
A count of 1 in mode 2 or 3 is stored as 0x10001.
A new count restarts the count at once, with no wait for a CLK pulse.
The two halves of the wave are equal, so an odd count gives equal high and low times.
The counter value comes from the ticks elapsed since the count started, with no load pulse in between.
A new count restarts the count at once, with no wait for a CLK pulse.
A trigger restarts the count at once, with no wait for a CLK pulse.
A count of 0 is 0x10000 or 10000 BCD and a count of 1 in mode 2 or 3 is 0x10001.
A GATE change acts at once, with no sampling on a CLK edge.
Counting is computed from elapsed time, with no CLK edge on which counts load or decrement.
A trigger loads the count and sets OUT low at once, with no wait for a CLK pulse.
A rising GATE sets OUT high and reloads the count at once, with no wait for a CLK pulse.
A GATE trigger sets OUT and reloads the count at once, with no wait for a CLK pulse.
A rising GATE edge acts at once, with no flip-flop sampled on the next CLK edge.
Read handlers are installed on ports 0x40 to 0x42, write handlers on 0x40, 0x42 and 0x43, none for a write to 0x41.
A rising GATE edge triggers mode 3 only while the clock input is stopped.
In modes 1 and 5 a timed-out counter reads a constant 0xFFFF and does not go on counting.
